bug_semantics: DNSIncoming._decode_labels_at_offset recurses once per RFC 1035 §4.1.4 DNS-name compression pointer. Cycle detection (seen_pointers) and MAX_DNS_LABELS=128 capped repeated offsets and label count, but a chain of unique forward pointers that add no extra labels was unbounded. A single ~3 kB mDNS datagram with ~1500 such pointers exceeds CPython's default recursion limit. DECODE_EXCEPTIONS was (IndexError, struct.error, IncomingDecodeError) and omitted RecursionError, so the exception escaped DNSIncoming.__init__ to asyncio's default handler. Any unauthenticated host on the local link (UDP/5353, 224.0.0.251 / ff02::fb) can force sustained CPU burn and log flooding.
flaw_origin: The pre-#934 decoder in DNSIncoming.read_name was an iterative while-True loop that followed only backward pointers (off >= first raised IncomingDecodeError) and never recursed. PR #934 rewrote that loop to accept forward compression pointers. First-write member 0a36cc6815a7c6593b249242a6854e1a7ca3b590 added DnsNameReader._decode_labels_at_offset with an uncached recursive call at zeroconf/_protocol.py:133 and DECODE_EXCEPTIONS without RecursionError. 15a89a0ed8b9ba61814ba15d0b573c556cbc44c5 collapsed the helper into DNSIncoming (a move, not a first write). GitHub squash 5682a4c3c89043bf8a10e79232933ada5ab71972 landed the same recursive mechanism on master and shipped in 0.33.3. No pointer-chain depth cap existed until PR #1719.

reasoning: The advisory and CVE-2026-47180 are live published records of CWE-674 unbounded recursion in the mDNS name-compression decoder, not withdrawn or rejected, so this is a real vulnerability. The attack is a unique forward pointer chain that never repeats an offset (so seen_pointers never fires) and never accumulates 128 labels (so MAX_DNS_LABELS never fires), driving Python recursion past sys.getrecursionlimit while RecursionError bypasses DECODE_EXCEPTIONS. Pickaxe of _decode_labels_at_offset and the parent tree at 4d30c25 show the recursive follow was not original: tag 0.33.2 still used an iterative backward-only loop.
